candidates.title: Draft logistics event notices

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a dispatcher notification when a shipment is delayed, using a supplied shipment status.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: A simple flow can notify a dispatcher when a shipment is delayed

candidates.whoPays: Hypothesis: small ecommerce operators or logistics service firms that coordinate shipments might pay for reviewed exception notices; the discussion establishes no buying intent or payment.

experimentPlan.output: A draft dispatcher notice and a short reason when a supplied fictional shipment row meets a manually chosen delay rule.
inputs: Fictional expected and latest status timestamps
experimentPlan.trigger: A student manually submits a fictional shipment row for review.
steps: Enter a fictional shipment row and the operator chosen delay threshold.
Check whether the row crosses that threshold.
Draft a dispatcher notice with the shipment identifier and status.
Show the rule and input values beside the draft.
Ask a person to verify the status and approve any real message outside the prototype.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a small set of fictional rows with manually labeled delayed or not delayed outcomes, the displayed flag and notice draft match the labels and expose the values used.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person chooses the threshold, supplies trustworthy shipment data, confirms whether a delay is real, and approves any communication; no carrier access or message sending is included.
unverified: The source gives an example but no customer specific fields, delay rules, recurrence, or corroboration.
No supplied implementation reference supports shipment data access or message delivery.

ease.reason: A fictional row and manually chosen rule make a review mock approachable; the attached discussion provides no implementation support for intake or notices.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small ecommerce or logistics operators might value reviewed delay notices; this example establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week fictional-row mock is bounded, but the source supplies no fields, business threshold, live data access, or delivery support.

autonomy.reason: A proposed rule can draft repeatable notices from supplied rows, but a person must verify shipment status and approve communication; execution is unsupported.

evidence.reason: One retained task span names delayed-shipment notices as an example; frequency, fields, a specific buyer, and corroboration are absent from these spans.

candidates.reason: Concrete example assessed with a narrow proposed mock; its provisional mean is below six because demand is a single example and no implementation or buyer evidence is supplied.

candidates.title: Review mobile game test CSV logs

demandEvidence.chore: Transfer mobile game test measurements from a notes app CSV into a Google Sheet and avoid missed or repeated file processing.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Right now I type it into a notes app during the session, then later export a CSV from that app and paste it into a Google Sheet.

candidates.whoPays: Hypothesis: independent mobile game testers or small game testing teams might pay for a cleaner log review and import aid; this post establishes no buying intent or payment.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed table of supplied game test CSV rows with repeated rows marked and the chosen comparison fields shown.
inputs: Synthetic CSV rows with battery percentage, device temperature, frame drops, and a short session note
Student chosen fields for duplicate comparison
Expected row labels for a test batch
experimentPlan.trigger: A tester manually selects a CSV export and submits it to a local review prototype.
steps: Extract CSV data into row objects using the documented n8n extraction node (5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74).
Apply the tester selected comparison fields to mark repeated rows using the documented duplicate removal operations (f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108).
Display retained and flagged rows with the selected fields.
Have a tester verify the marks before manually importing any rows into a sheet.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For a synthetic CSV fixture with expected repeated rows labeled in advance, each repeated row is flagged according to the selected fields and the remaining measurement values are preserved for human review.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A tester exports and supplies the file, selects meaningful comparison fields, checks every flagged or retained row, and performs any Sheet import; no phone trigger or live Sheet write is proposed.
unverified: The post describes one person's workflow; demand beyond this post and willingness to pay are unknown.
The supplied n8n references support CSV row extraction and duplicate operations, but not the phone upload trigger or Google Sheets import in this proposed flow.
The right comparison fields and CSV variations require tester input and validation.

ease.reason: n8n docs support CSV-to-row extraction (5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74) and configurable duplicate comparison (f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108); phone intake remains outside scope.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent game testers might pay to reduce log cleanup; the discussion identifies a manual task but no purchase intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic CSV review fits the documented extraction (5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74) and deduplication (f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108) operations; actual file variations need checking.

autonomy.reason: The references 5c2bf4e7df8c3ec325ba2e74 and f1662b0ceb942474f83a8108 support repeatable extraction and row comparison; a tester chooses fields, submits files, reviews results, and imports manually.

evidence.reason: The retained spans describe manual measurement logging, later CSV transfer, and a trigger that misses or repeats files; this is one post with no corroboration.

candidates.reason: The task and bounded scope are concrete, and supplied n8n documentation supports CSV extraction and duplicate comparison; the provisional mean is 5.4, below six, with live intake, correct matching fields, and payment unresolved.

candidates.title: Compare daily Shopify order exports

demandEvidence.chore: Export daily Shopify orders for the same 30-day period, limited to Online Store and excluding test and cancelled orders, for comparison with ad purchase counts.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: In Shopify, export daily orders for the same 30 days, Online Store channel only, without test and cancelled orders.

candidates.whoPays: Hypothesis: small online shops or independent ecommerce advisers might pay for a clearer daily ad-sales comparison; the post establishes no buying intent or payment.

experimentPlan.output: A date-aligned comparison table of two operator-supplied daily purchase exports that flags differing totals without claiming why they differ.
inputs: Synthetic daily Shopify Online Store order counts
Operator supplied exclusion labels for test and cancelled orders
experimentPlan.trigger: A shop operator manually supplies two matching-period CSV exports to a prototype.
steps: Enter two synthetic daily count tables for the same date range.
Check date coverage and mark missing dates.
Compare the supplied counts by date.
Flag dates with different totals without assigning a cause.
Show the inputs and exclusions so a person can inspect and interpret the results.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Given a fixture with known dates, counts, and missing dates, the output aligns dates correctly, flags each count difference and missing date, and never labels the cause as proven.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person exports and filters the records, confirms date range and channel, interprets attribution differences, and investigates tracking; no account connection, tax analysis, or automatic fix is included.
unverified: The supplied post gives instructions and possible explanations, but demand recurrence and buyer intent are unknown.
No supplied implementation reference supports exports, account access, or a live integration.
Correct handling of actual export formats and attribution requires human validation.

ease.reason: A synthetic date-by-date table is a manageable mock, but the discussion provides no implementation support for exports or live account access.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small shops or ecommerce advisers might pay for clearer comparisons; one instructional post establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week supplied-file mock is bounded, but actual export formats and reliable date/channel mapping are not documented in these spans.

autonomy.reason: A proposed comparison can flag dates from supplied counts, but people must export, filter, interpret causes, and investigate tracking; no automation support is attached.

evidence.reason: The retained spans specify export filters, explain normal and unusual count gaps, and describe a test event check; recurrence and corroboration are absent.

candidates.reason: The instructions support a bounded comparison experiment, but not validated buyer demand, a live integration, or recurring need; provisional mean is 4.8, below six.
